title: "fx-vrp"
subtitle: "The FX variance risk premium: jump risk, discrete hedging error, and transaction costs"
date: 2026-05-01

::: {.status}
Still in progress. The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/NavyBlueCheese/fx-vrp).
:::

Currency options usually price in more variance than the market ends up
delivering. That gap is the variance risk premium (VRP). This project
asks two separate questions about it:

1. Is the premium paid for jump and crash risk, or for ordinary
   day-to-day (diffusive) risk?
2. Can anyone actually collect it once delta-hedging happens at discrete
   intervals and trading costs are realistic?

The second question matters because selling a straddle and delta-hedging
it doesn't earn the raw gap between implied and realised variance. It
earns a gamma-weighted version of that gap,

$$\Pi \approx \int_0^T \tfrac12\,\Gamma_u S_u^2\left(\sigma^2_{\text{implied}} - \sigma^2_{\text{realised},u}\right)du,$$

so *when* the realised variance arrives, relative to where the option's
gamma sits, decides the P&L.

The implied leg comes from CBOE's EuroCurrency volatility index (EVZ),
replicated from option chains with the VIX methodology. The realised
leg is built from Dukascopy tick data over the same 30-calendar-day
window, with both legs stamped at 16:15 New York so nothing from later in
the day leaks into a signal.

| Phase | What it covers | State |
|:-:|---------------|:--|
| 0 | Data reconnaissance and fixed conventions | done |
| 1 | Simulators, tick/rates/option-chain data layer, daily chain scraper | done |
| 2 | Realised-variance estimators, validated on simulated ground truth | done |
| 3 | Implied variance: model-free IV, VIX replication | done |
| 4 | The VRP series: HAR forecasts, ex-ante vs ex-post | in progress |
| 5 | Strategy, P&L attribution, hedging-frequency study | next |

Conventions, data notes, and the phase reports are in the repository's
`docs/` folder.
